pages.text: *CLUNK* Auto-Strapper arms deploy at eight distinct points. You're secured firmly to what appears to be a changing table. Just… appearing out of the floor.
CHANGING TABLE: DEPLOYED. This unit has been waiting for a visitor. The last three adventurers didn't even make it past the antechamber. You should feel accomplished. Now hold still.
TUG DETECTED. *straps tighten significantly* The Naughty Protocol has engaged. You will now receive the Deluxe Package. Congratulations on upgrading.
Oh yes. They are all residents now. Very happy residents. Babbling quite a bit more than before. You'd probably describe it as a downgrade. The unit describes it as a very successful outcome.
Waiting detected. Respectful. *The table's surface begins to warm* You will find the process much more pleasant if you cooperate. Or unpleasant if you don't. Both outcomes end the same way.
Auto-Strapper Unit looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Auto-Strapper Unit tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Auto-Strapper Unit catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Auto-Strapper Unit laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

Seven minutes. You were strapped to the Auto-Strapper's table for seven minutes.

In those seven minutes:

Every item of clothing you arrived in was removed, catalogued, and deposited in a chute labelled DISPOSAL. Your arms, legs, torso, and head were held perfectly still by padded restraints that adjusted their grip in real-time to prevent even the smallest movement. The table's surface warmed to exactly body temperature — comfortable, in the way that a trap is comfortable.

Then the dressing began.

An auto-locking bonnet was placed on your head first. Then a snap-crotch nursery coverall. Then — and this is the part you will think about in quiet moments for the rest of your life — the largest diaper you have ever seen was positioned beneath you, pulled between your legs, and sealed with tabs that locked with an audible *click*.

The diaper is enormous. Maximum absorbency. Designed for what the Machine calls 'extended unsupervised periods.' It forces your legs so far apart that walking will require a waddle so pronounced it might technically qualify as a new gait.

Locked bloomers were pulled over the diaper. The word 'locked' is doing real work in that sentence — there is a physical lock, a small chrome mechanism that clicked shut over your hip and will not open without a key that is certainly not in this room.

Activity socks — the kind with bells sewn to them — were slid onto your feet with mechanical precision. Nursery booties followed. A foam mallet was pressed into your hand because the Machine couldn't find anything more infantilising that still technically counted as a weapon.

The straps released.

You sat up slowly on the changing table. Everything crinkled. Everything jingled. The bonnet sat heavy and warm on your head. The coverall pulled across your chest. The diaper beneath the locked bloomers was so thick you could feel it pressing against the table surface like a cushion.

The Machine's display read: PROCEDURE COMPLETE. HAVE A NICE DAY.

You slid off the table. Your feet hit the floor with a double-jingle. The waddle began immediately.

*The massive slime SURGES toward you, its body sloshing with gallons of warm, enchanted milk. It's three times bigger than a normal Bottle Slime.*
*GLORPPP* *The Bloated Slime engulfs you entirely. Warm milk floods in from every direction. You can feel its body vibrating with a deep, satisfied BABA...*
*The slime doesn't understand words. It only understands FEEDING. It crashes over you like a warm, milky tidal wave.*

*You lose count of how many bottles' worth of milk you swallowed. Your belly is painfully full and the pressure in your bladder is UNBEARABLE. The slime finally releases you with a content BABA~ and oozes away.*
*Struggling only makes the slime squeeze tighter, forcing more milk into you. By the time it lets go, you're drenched, bloated, and something is already happening that you can't stop...*
Bloated Bottle Slime looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Bloated Bottle Slime tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Bloated Bottle Slime catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Bloated Bottle Slime laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

You surface.

That's the only word for it — you *surface*, like someone pulled from a warm, milk-white ocean. Coughing. Spluttering. Your entire body drenched in enchanted formula that pools around you on the forest floor in a spreading white lake.

Your belly is enormous. Not metaphorically — literally, visibly, alarmingly distended. You look down and can barely see past the swollen dome of your stomach to where the Bloated Slime helpfully sealed you in cobweb padding and plugged you shut during the engulfing.

The pacifier is still lodged in your mouth. The slime put it there while you were drowning in milk, and the sucking reflex it triggers is the only thing that kept your airway clear. Your body learned to nurse from it on pure survival instinct, and now it won't stop.

The math is horrible and you can feel every number.

Gallons of enchanted milk inside you. A mushroom plug ensuring nothing exits from one end. A bladder operating at what feels like two hundred percent capacity. Cobweb padding fastened around hips that are already struggling to contain everything the slime force-fed you.

The pressure is *astronomical*.

Something is going to give. Multiple somethings. Your body makes a wet, gurgling sound that starts in your stomach and travels downward with unstoppable momentum. The cobweb diaper crinkles — then *expands* slightly, its enchanted fibres stretching to accommodate what's coming.

The Bloated Slime gurgles a satisfied *BABA~* from somewhere in the forest canopy. You can feel it watching.

You take one step. Your belly sloshes. Your bladder screams. The plug holds firm. The only exit left is the one the cobweb padding was designed for.

And it is the most thorough, sustained, unstoppable loss of control you have ever experienced in your life.

Your belly is enormous. Not metaphorically — literally, visibly, alarmingly distended. You look down and can barely see past the swollen dome of your stomach to where the Bloated Slime helpfully sealed you in cobweb padding and plugged you shut during the engulfing.

The pacifier is still lodged in your mouth. The slime put it there while you were drowning in milk, and the sucking reflex it triggers is the only thing that kept your airway clear. Your body learned to nurse from it on pure survival instinct, and now it won't stop.

The math is horrible and you can feel every number.

Gallons of enchanted milk inside you. A mushroom plug ensuring nothing exits from one end. A bladder operating at what feels like two hundred percent capacity. Cobweb padding fastened around hips that are already struggling to contain everything the slime force-fed you.

The pressure is *astronomical*.

Something is going to give. Multiple somethings. Your body makes a wet, gurgling sound that starts in your stomach and travels downward with unstoppable momentum. The cobweb diaper crinkles — then *expands* slightly, its enchanted fibres stretching to accommodate what's coming.

The Bloated Slime gurgles a satisfied *BABA~* from somewhere in the forest canopy. You can feel it watching.

You take one step. Your belly sloshes. Your bladder screams. The plug holds firm. The only exit left is the one the cobweb padding was designed for.

And it is the most thorough, sustained, unstoppable loss of control you have ever experienced in your life.

*gloop gloop* ...Baba? Baba baba!
*The Bottle Slime oozes over you and shoves its nipple-shaped top toward your mouth*
*The slime jiggles, offended* Baba!! BABA!! *It sloshes warm milk all over you*
*Warm, slightly sweet milk fills your mouth. It tastes... actually kind of nice. The slime pats your head with a pseudopod.* Baba~
*The slime clings tighter, gurgling happily. It's not letting go until you finish your bottle. All of it.* Baba baba!
Bottle Slime looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Bottle Slime tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Bottle Slime catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Bottle Slime laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

You lie on the dungeon floor, gasping. The Bottle Slime has oozed away, leaving you drenched in warm, faintly sweet milk that's rapidly cooling on your skin and soaking into your clothes. But the real damage is inside.

Your belly is distended. Painfully, visibly swollen with the sheer volume of enchanted milk the slime forced into you. Every breath pushes your stomach outward and you can hear the liquid sloshing inside — a wet, gurgling symphony of fullness that you can feel in your teeth.

The pacifier it jammed between your lips is still there, and the gentle sucking reflex it triggers sends tiny pulses of comfort through your body that contrast grotesquely with the churning in your gut.

The pressure is building already. So much liquid, all of it enchanted, all of it rushing through your system with supernatural efficiency. Your bladder was at maybe thirty percent before the fight. Now it feels like a water balloon stretched to its absolute limit — tight, hot, aching, and searingly urgent.

You need a toilet. You need one now. You needed one five minutes ago.

You struggle to your feet. Your tummy gurgles ominously. Something below the tummy gurgles worse. The slime's milk has soaked your continence from the inside out, and you can feel the weakness spreading — muscles that should be clenched tight doing barely anything, gates that should be shut barely holding.

You waddle forward, one hand on your distended belly, the pacifier bobbing with each desperate step. The wet sounds your body makes follow you like a warning.

Bzz-bzz, there we are, all tuckered out! Nanny's got you, sweet pea.
*Two of its six stubby arms hold you still while the other four busy themselves at your waistband.* Now, a little check, shall we? Nanny always checks.
Bzz! Every little flower in Nanny's meadow is a sweet pea. Even the grumpy ones. *Especially* the grumpy ones.
Out here is the best place! Lots of fresh air, lots of sunshine! *It lifts your waistband and peeks, humming loud enough for the whole field to hear.* Mmhm. Mm-HM. Just as Nanny thought.
Good girl. Arms up, that's it. *There's a rustle of crinkly padding and the very businesslike sound of tapes.*
*When it finally buzzes off, you're wearing a fresh printed diaper and a big frilly bow tied into your hair with a very firm knot.* Bzz! Nanny will be back to check on you later!
Bumble Nanny looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Bumble Nanny tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Bumble Nanny catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Bumble Nanny laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

Worst of all is the echo of that humming "Mm-HM", loud enough for the whole meadow to hear, and the way a pair of passing adventurers suddenly found the sky very interesting.

aftermaths.title: Defeat - Bumble Nanny (Variation B): Nanny Knows Best

pages.text:
You try to argue with the tapes and lose. You try to argue with the bow and lose. Somewhere behind you, the Bumble Nanny is humming a lullaby to the clover.

The diaper is thick and soft and warm, and the part of you that's been clenching all day quietly notices that nothing bad would happen now if you just... stopped clenching. You keep walking. You keep noticing.

aftermaths.title: Defeat - Bumble Nanny (Variation C): Back Later

pages.text:
"Nanny will be back to check on you later!"

You make it almost to the village gate before the thought of being checked again, out here, with everyone watching, makes your stomach flip. The flip travels downward. By the time you notice, the fresh diaper isn't fresh any more, and you have the awful certainty that Nanny will know.
Bumble Nanny studies you with an unsettling sense of recognition. 'We've done this before, haven't we?'
'Your body remembers even if you won't admit it. I can see the evidence.'
'Again and again, if that's what it takes. You'll learn.'
'Wrong? Look at yourself. Really look. Then tell me I'm wrong.'
'Smart. It goes easier when you stop pretending.'

The buzzing fades over the hill, but the feeling of being checked doesn't. Your new diaper crinkles with every step. The bow won't come undone; Nanny tied it with a knot you don't recognise.

Worst of all is the echo of that humming "Mm-HM", loud enough for the whole meadow to hear, and the way a pair of passing adventurers suddenly found the sky very interesting.

*The Cinder Slime flows over your legs, heavy and warm as bathwater, and settles in your lap with a contented blorp.*

actions.label: Get off, you are so HOT!

pages.text: *It doesn't move. It just gets warmer. Sweat runs down your back, your legs, everywhere, until you can't tell what's sweat and what isn't.*
*It purrs, somehow, with a sound like a kettle. The warmth soaks through you and your whole body goes slack.* Blorp.
*The slime jiggles in a way that feels an awful lot like a shrug. When it finally oozes off, it leaves you in a fresh, thick diaper and a very suspicious warmth.*
*Eventually it slides away to find another warm rock, leaving you padded, steaming and very, very damp.*
Cinder Slime looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Cinder Slime tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Cinder Slime catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Cinder Slime laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'
Some of it was sweat. You're almost sure some of it was sweat. The thick diaper the slime left you in is heavy and warm, and it isn't all from the slime.
Your legs are still sticky and your clothes are clinging to you. Everything is damp, everything is warm, and your body seems to have decided that damp and warm is a signal.
You squelch as you walk. Squelch, squelch, squelch. There is no dignified way to squelch.
Cinder Slime studies you with an unsettling sense of recognition. 'We've done this before, haven't we?'
'Your body remembers even if you won't admit it. I can see the evidence.'
'Again and again, if that's what it takes. You'll learn.'
'Wrong? Look at yourself. Really look. Then tell me I'm wrong.'
'Smart. It goes easier when you stop pretending.'

*CREEEEAK* The Cradle Golem unfolds its bars with terrible slowness. What you thought was a decorative crib in the corner was, in fact, a predator.
*The Golem wraps a bar around your ankle with surprising tenderness.* REST. The bars are enchanted. They know when a little one needs to sleep. And you... the reading is quite high.
*The Golem's bars extend across the floor like a net. You trip.* No running in the nursery. *says it exactly like a tired parent* The rule is three hundred years old. Please cooperate.

Disagreed. *The slats close gently.* The Cradle Golem has held adventurers since the nursery's founding. None of them needed sleep when they arrived. All of them did within one lullaby. You will be changed and comfortable very shortly.
Yes. *satisfied creak* This is by design. You will find the padding quite comfortable too. The enchantments ensure a proper night's sleep and a properly attended-to morning. You need not fight it.
Cradle Golem looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'

'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'

'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'

'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

The Cradle Golem rocks you.

Not violently. Not mechanically. With the slow, steady, patient rhythm of something that has been rocking children to sleep since before the dungeon had a name. Its wooden bars creak softly — almost musically — and the warm enchantment radiating from its ancient frame seeps into your bones like heated honey.

You're wearing a flutter-hem tutu now. You don't remember putting it on. The Maximum Absorbency Diaper is taped underneath — you DEFINITELY don't remember that happening, but you can feel it. Oh, you can feel it. It's enormous. A warm, crinkly presence between your thighs that forces your legs apart and makes every micro-movement a production of rustling sounds. Nursery booties are buckled to your feet, soft-soled and warm.

The Golem's lullaby is doing something to you. It's not just soothing — it's *enchanting*, in the literal sense. Your eyelids droop. Your thoughts soften. The fight, the defeat, the humiliation of being cradled and changed by a living piece of furniture — all of it blurs at the edges, becoming distant, becoming a dream.

You sleep.

When you wake, you don't know how much time has passed. It could be minutes. It could be hours. You're inside the Golem — behind its bars, in its cradle basin — warm, rested, and with a bladder that has been filling the entire time you were unconscious.

The pressure is immediate and desperate. Your body relaxed completely during the enchanted sleep, and in those hours of unconsciousness, your control relaxed too. You can feel the warm evidence of that relaxation already in the thick padding — the diaper has been working while you slept.

The Golem's bars open with a gentle creak. It says nothing. It doesn't need to.

You climb out of the crib. Everything crinkles. Everything is warm. The lullaby's echo still hums in your chest.

actions.label: Don't look at me like that.

pages.text: Purple light blooms beneath your skin, warm and dizzying. Your pulse races until you can barely think.
"Control is only another mask," the cultist says, brushing your cheek. The heat surges even higher.
"Feel it all," the cultist whispers. A rush of body magic leaves your excitement meter near bursting.
Cultist of Excite looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Cultist of Excite tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Cultist of Excite catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Cultist of Excite laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

The Cultist of Excite touches your temples with two fingers and *pushes*.

Not physically. Metaphysically. They push something directly into the part of your brain that produces excitement — the ventral striatum, the reward pathways, the deep limbic alchemy that turns 'interesting' into 'overwhelming' — and they crank it to eleven.

Everything becomes vivid and terrible and too much. The candlelight in the mansion hall is *blinding*. The sound of your own breathing is *thunderous*. The sensation of your own clothing against your skin is an absolute sensory emergency — every thread, every seam, every patch of fabric pressing against you is amplified to the threshold of unbearable.

Including the padding they just slid between your legs. You feel every molecule of it. Its texture. Its warmth. Its bulk. The way it presses against you from all angles, encasing and containing and very definitely present.

Your excitement surges.

Not abstract excitement — quantified, clinical, game-mechanical excitement. The cultist's gift is the exact variety of overstimulation that sends your shame fleeing and your excite meter climbing with every second. Your face feels hot. Your heart pounds. The bonnet's ribbons tickling your neck are somehow the most vivid sensation you've ever experienced.

The thin, frilly dress that was fitted over you while your senses were overloaded rustles with the weight of a thunderstorm. The bloomers swish. Everything swishes, crinkles, presses, touches, and your nervous system processes it all at maximum volume.

The Cultist of Excite stands back and watches you process the world at unbearable intensity. Their expression is that of an audiophile who just plugged a speaker in wrong and blew the amplifier — awe mixed with a thin satisfaction.

'The Excite speaks through sensation,' they say. 'Every feeling is holy.'

The padding is very holy right now. Your bladder, already destabilised by the overstimulated signals flooding your nervous system, contributes a warm tide of holiness to it with the inevitability of a dam at capacity.

The Cultist makes a note in their ledger — something about 'response time: immediate' — and nods, satisfied.

The padding is very holy right now. Your bladder, already destabilised by the overstimulated signals flooding your nervous system, contributes a warm tide of holiness to it with the inevitability of a dam at capacity.

The Cultist makes a note in their ledger — something about 'response time: immediate' — and nods, satisfied.

The gifts are: explosive cramping, a belly so distended you can see it moving, complete loss of voluntary bowel control, and the blessed certainty that for the next many turns your body will serve the Tum whether you consent or not. The thick padding registers its first sacred offering almost immediately.

The cultist places their palms on your rounded belly one more time. The warmth intensifies. Another blessed gurgle rolls through you.

'Blessed be the Tum,' they whisper.

Your body responds in the language of the faithful.

The divine moisture continues its circuit for many turns. The padding accepts it all.

They dress you with the focussed attention of someone performing a baptism — smoothing the ghostweave fabric over your shoulders, snapping the onesie's crotch buttons one by one, then pulling the luminescent bloomers upward to cover everything below your waist.

Beneath the onesie, under the bloomers: padding. Heavy, plush, glowing faintly with the same cold ghostlight as the rest of the ghost garments. It was already in place under you before the prayer began, applied during the fight's final moments when you were too distracted to notice.

Your bladder sends one last message to your brain. Your brain replies that it is doing its absolute best. The cultist places a gentle hand on your lower belly — just a touch, just a moment of pressure — and says, very softly: 'The Blessed Flow accepts all offerings.'

You become an offering.

The warmth spreads through the padding in concentric rings, absorbed with quiet dignity by the ghost-woven absorbent material. The bloomers' luminescence brightens slightly. The cultist smiles with the transcendent peace of the devout.

The divine moisture continues its circuit for many turns. The padding accepts it all.

Hee hee! Bless you! Bless you! BLESS YOU!
But you're so much fun to puff at! Every time you sneeze you do the little knee-squeeze. Like this! *It crosses its tiny stem-legs and wobbles.*
*The sneeze takes you by surprise. So does the little warm leak that comes with it.* Ooh! Hee hee, bless you twice!
*The sprite puffs one last fluffy cloud right under your nose. You sneeze. You squeeze. Your knees knock together all on their own.* ...You do, though.
Okay, okay! One more for luck! *PFFF* ...Oops. That one was a big one, huh? Better find some bushes, bless-you-girl! *It tucks a dandelion bow into your hair and bounces away giggling.*
Dandelion Sprite looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Dandelion Sprite tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Dandelion Sprite catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Dandelion Sprite laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

Your eyes stream. Your nose tickles. Fluffy seeds are stuck in your hair, your collar, your eyelashes. Every few steps another sneeze builds, and every sneeze squeezes your very full bladder like a fist.

The sprite's pollen did something. You needed to go before the fight. Now you need to go the way you needed to go when you were small: suddenly, completely, right now.

*Ah... ah... ACHOO.*

That one does it. A hot spurt escapes before you can clamp down, and then another with the next sneeze. You end up bent double in the long grass, sneezing and leaking and sneezing again, while far away a tiny voice giggles "Bless youuu!"

aftermaths.title: Defeat - Dandelion Sprite (Variation B): Knee Squeeze

pages.text:
You walk back along the trail doing exactly what the sprite said you do: the little knee-squeeze. Every tickle in your nose makes your thighs clench and your hand drift toward your lap.

You catch your reflection in a rain barrel. You look like a toddler doing a potty dance in the middle of a field, with a dandelion bow in your hair.

aftermaths.title: Defeat - Dandelion Sprite (Variation C): Seeds Everywhere

pages.text: You find seeds in your clothes for the rest of the day, and each one sets off another sneeze. On the third, your body gives up the fight entirely. It isn't a big accident, just a steady, helpless dribble while you stand there sniffling, but it doesn't stop until it's finished.
Dandelion Sprite studies you with an unsettling sense of recognition. 'We've done this before, haven't we?'

'Wrong? Look at yourself. Really look. Then tell me I'm wrong.'
'Smart. It goes easier when you stop pretending.'

THWACK.

The sound echoes down the corridor. Then silence. Then the soft, settling crinkle of industrial-grade adhesive diaper tabs achieving what the manufacturer's label describes as MAXIMUM BONDING.

You look down. The auto-taped diaper is sealed around your hips with the precision of a machine that was designed to do exactly one thing and has had decades of practice doing it perfectly. The tabs aren't just stuck — they're molecularly fused. You could chip at them with a chisel and they'd laugh at you.

Your old underwear is gone. Vaporised somewhere during the impact. In its place: a cursed, auto-sealed, medical-grade nursery diaper that hums with a faint vibration you can feel in your hip bones.

Activity socks jingle on your feet. You didn't even feel those land.

The Diaper Dispenser Bot sits motionless in its wall alcove, seventeen remaining rounds visible in its loading bay. Its status light pulses a satisfied green.

PATIENT STATUS: SECURED. DIAPER INTEGRITY: 100%. ESTIMATED USAGE WINDOW: 4-6 HOURS BASED ON CURRENT INCONTINENCE METRICS.

The bot knows your incontinence level. Of course it does. It scanned you on approach. That's why it used the heavy-duty model with the reinforced backing and the extra-wide absorbent core. It calculated exactly how much protection you need and applied it with zero margin for error.

You take a step. The diaper crinkles. The activity socks jingle. Together they form a duet of humiliation that will follow you through every corridor, every encounter, every moment until you find authorised nursery equipment to release the tabs.

The bot said a NannyBot could remove them.

You've met the NannyBot. It will not remove them. It will add more.

A deep, insistent ache bloomed in your lower belly, a magical command that demanded release without warning, bypassing the will that had held you steady for so long. You clenched your fists, trying to hold the tide, but the magic was a tide of its own, rising to meet your resistance. You felt the first warmth spread through the layers, a heavy, soaking heat that seeped into the padding, binding you to the dungeon floor in a sticky, surrendered silence. The shame was a cold fire now, burning behind your eyes, as you realized the magic wasn't just a trap; it was a promise that you would never stand tall again.

4.7 minutes. That's how long the Formula Feeder Bot held you. You know because its chest display counted down in bright blue numerals while the nozzle delivered a continuous stream of warm, sweet formula directly into you.

Your stomach is bloated. Painfully, dangerously, *audibly* bloated. You can hear the formula sloshing inside with every breath — a gurgling, churning sound that's part washing machine, part angry ocean, part biological warning klaxon.

The bot patted your head when it was done. Once. A single, mechanical pat. Then it rolled back to its charging station, its feeding nozzle retracting with a satisfied *click*.

The formula hits your system like a warm, liquid freight train in slow motion.

First your stomach protests — a deep, rolling cramp that makes you double over. Then the liquid begins to move downward with the inevitability of gravity and enchanted nutrition, filling spaces you didn't know could fill, pressing against walls that are already struggling.

Your bladder was minding its own business before the feeding. Now it's a emergency reservoir for approximately three times more liquid than it was designed to hold, and the pressure is *increasing* by the second as the enchanted formula processes with supernatural speed.

The nursery nappy taped around you — applied at some point during the feeding, you were too busy trying to breathe — suddenly feels less like an indignity and more like an urgent engineering necessity.

Your body makes a wet, decisive sound. The nappy responds. The formula does not stop processing.

4.7 minutes of input. Hours of output. The math is inescapable.

pages.text: They guide you into a sitting position and begin to speak — low, measured, with the cadence of someone who has talked a thousand panicking people through a thousand panicking moments. "Focus on my voice. Not on what's happening. Not on what happened. Just my voice."

"Don't I?" They tap two fingers against your forehead. A pulse of calm radiates from the point of contact. "Your body is telling me everything, little one. The tension. The shame spiral. The way you keep pulling at your clothes hoping nobody notices. I see all of it."

"You don't have to *want* to. That's the beautiful thing about trance." Their voice drops half an octave. "The part of you that's exhausted from fighting this — from fighting your *body* — it's already listening. It's been waiting for permission to stop clenching."

Warmth floods through you like sinking into a bath. The Hypnotist's voice becomes the only sound in the mansion.

"Your body does what it does. That's not failure — that's just biology being honest. The padding is there to help, not to punish. The accidents aren't your fault. The feelings aren't wrong. You are a person dealing with something difficult, and you are doing it beautifully."

Your eyes close. The shame that's been coiled in your chest like a spring... quietly unwinds.
Adept Hypnotist looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Adept Hypnotist tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Adept Hypnotist catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Adept Hypnotist laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

The Adept Hypnotist catches you as you fall and lowers you to the ground with practised care. No fumbling. No hesitation. Their hands arrange you into a comfortable seated position against the mansion wall as if they've done this hundreds of times — because they have.

'There,' they say. 'That's better. Now close your eyes.'

You don't close your eyes. Not intentionally. It just happens. The Adept's voice has a weight to it — a warm gravitational pull that bypasses your conscious mind entirely and speaks directly to something older, deeper, more tired. The part of you that has been *holding* — holding your bladder, holding your composure, holding the fraying edges of your dignity together with white-knuckled desperation — exhales.

The trance is nothing like the Novice's tentative pendant-swing. This is architecture. The Adept builds it around you like walls — not to trap you, but to create a space where the pressure can finally let up. Layer by layer, the anxious noise dims. The shame-voice that narrates every accident, every near-miss, every waddling step gets quieter and quieter until it's barely a whisper.

'I want you to think about the last time you had an accident,' the Adept says. Their voice is a warm hand on a fevered forehead. 'Not the facts of it. The *feeling* of it. The heat in your face. The panic. The way you checked to see if anyone saw. The way you felt *less* because your body did what bodies do.'

Your face burns. But distantly. The trance holds you at one safe remove from the memory.

'Now I want you to forgive yourself for that. Not because it wasn't embarrassing. It was. But because embarrassment is not a life sentence. Because your body was not betraying you — it was being honest. And honesty deserves grace, not punishment.'

The words sink in. Not intellectually — deeper than that. Into the place where shame lives, where it's been building layers of sediment for every wet morning, every failed sprint to the bathroom, every time you felt the telltale warmth and knew you hadn't made it.

The Adept's trance doesn't remove those memories. It reframes them. One by one, like turning pictures to face a gentler light.

*You had an accident in the dungeon. Your padding caught it. You kept going. That took courage.*

*You woke up wet. You changed. You continued your day. That took resilience.*

*Someone noticed the bulk under your clothes. You survived the moment. That took strength you didn't know you had.*

Each reframe loosens something. Like undoing knots you didn't know were there — knots in your shoulders, your jaw, your pelvic floor, the constant clenching that had become so routine you'd forgotten what being relaxed felt like.

The Adept brings you back slowly. No sharp edges. No abrupt awakening. Just a gradual return to the cold stone and candlelight of the mansion, except everything feels... lighter.

Your excitement — the restless, nervous energy that had been building toward something unbearable — is completely gone. Reset to zero. In its place: a calm so deep it feels physical, like being wrapped in something warm and heavy.

The shame is still there. But thinner. Less like armour and more like gauze — something you can see through, breathe through, eventually shed.

'Take your time,' the Adept says, gathering their things. 'The trance fades, but the truth doesn't. You are allowed to be gentle with yourself.'

They leave. The corridor is quiet. You sit for a while, breathing, and notice with distant surprise that the padding between your legs doesn't make you flinch anymore. It's just there. Doing its job. Letting you do yours.

actions.label: Why are you looking at me like that?

pages.text: "Because you're ready." Their voice is devastating — silk over steel, tender and absolute. "You've been carrying something heavy for a very long time. You've been fighting your own body like it's the enemy. And you are so, so tired."
You can't. That's the first thing you discover about the Master Hypnotist — avoiding their gaze is like trying to un-hear a song. The trance has already begun. It began the moment they looked at you.

"The denial itself is the tiredness speaking." They place a single finger on your sternum. The touch is electric. "I can feel it. The exhaustion of pretending. The weight of every time you tried to hold it and couldn't. Every time you checked if someone noticed. Every quiet, private moment of shame that nobody saw but you carried anyway."

"Good." A single word, and with it, the trance deepens. The mansion disappears. The candles. The cold stone. All of it goes, replaced by a warm, dark nothing that holds you like a cradle.

"Now listen carefully, because I'm going to tell you something that will change how you feel about everything that's been happening to you."

You listen.

"Your incontinence is not a punishment. Not a curse. Not something broken inside you. It is your body being honest about what it needs. The padding between your legs isn't humiliation — it's care. It's someone, somewhere, acknowledging that you need help and providing it, without judgment."

The words settle into you like stones into still water.

"Every accident is your body saying: I don't have to hold this anymore. And that — that letting go — is the bravest thing a person can do."
Master Hypnotist looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Master Hypnotist tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Master Hypnotist catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Master Hypnotist laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

The Master Hypnotist does not catch you when you fall. They simply step into the space where you will land, and when you arrive there, you find yourself seated — gently, impossibly — as if gravity itself received new instructions.

They are already working.

Not speaking. Not yet. First comes the silence: a silence so complete, so *intentional*, that you realize the mansion's ambient noise — the dripping, the creaking, the distant whispers — has stopped. Or been stopped. The Master Hypnotist has drawn a boundary around this moment, and within it, nothing exists that they haven't invited.

Then: a single word.

'*Sleep.*'

Not a request. Not a suggestion. A statement of fact delivered to the deepest stratum of your consciousness, below the ego, below the defenses, below the exhausted, shame-wracked identity that has been running damage control since the first time your body surprisedyou in the worst possible way. The word bypasses all of it. You are asleep — not unconscious, not dreaming, but *held* in a state of profound, absolute surrender that you didn't know your mind was capable of.

The Master Hypnotist speaks into this space.

'I am going to dismantle something,' they say. 'It will not hurt. You built it to protect yourself, and it did its job, and now it is hurting you more than what it was protecting you from. I am talking about the shame.'

In the trance, you can *see* it. The shame. It's not an emotion down here — it's a structure. A vast, intricate scaffold of rules and reactions built one humiliation at a time. Every wet bed. Every failed hold. Every crinkle someone might have heard. Every time you looked down and saw the evidence of what your body had done without your permission. Each one became a brick. And the wall they built is enormous — a monument to the idea that your incontinence makes you less.

The Master Hypnotist walks up to the wall. They place one hand on it.

'This,' they say, 'is a lie.'

They don't tear it down. That would be violent. Instead, they show you what's behind it. On the other side of the shame is... you. Not a different you. Not a fixed-you or a cured-you. Just you — wearing what you're wearing, padded and maybe wet and certainly not what any manual of adulthood would prescribe — and *okay*. Not performing okayness. Not braving through it. Actually, genuinely, thoroughly okay.

'Your body lost the ability to wait,' the Master Hypnotist says, and their voice is the kindest thing you have ever heard. 'That is not a character flaw. It is not a punishment. It is not the universe's opinion of your worth. It is a medical reality, and you have been handling it with more grace than you give yourself credit for.

'The padding you wear is not a badge of failure. It is an adaptation. A tool. No different from glasses for poor eyesight or a cane for an unsteady leg. It lets you move through the world. It lets you keep going. It catches what you can't hold, and it does so without judgment, without complaint, without making you earn the right to be dry.

'Every accident you've had — every single one — was your body saying: *I cannot do this right now*. And every time, you kept going afterward. You changed, or you waited, or you simply continued with the warmth spreading and the knowledge that this is your life now, and you *lived through it*. That is not weakness. That is an act of ferocious, unglamorous bravery that no one will ever give you a medal for but that deserves one anyway.'

The wall doesn't crumble. It becomes transparent. You can see through it now — see through the shame to the person on the other side, and that person is looking back at you with an expression that you eventually recognize as compassion.

The Master Hypnotist withdraws their hand.

'When you wake up,' they say, 'you will remember everything I've said. Not as words — as truth. The shame will be quieter. Not gone — I'm a hypnotist, not a miracle worker — but quieter. Thin enough to see through. And the next time your body surprises you, the next time warmth spreads where you didn't want it to, the next time you hear the telltale crinkle or feel the telltale sag, I want you to hear my voice underneath the panic, saying: *this is okay. You are okay. You are allowed to exist exactly as you are.*'

A breath. A heartbeat. And then—

You're awake.

The mansion resolves around you. Stone and shadow and candlelight. The Master Hypnotist is already leaving, their footsteps silent on the flagstones. They don't look back. They don't need to. The work is done.

You sit in the quiet aftermath and take stock.

The excitement is gone. Not suppressed — genuinely absent, like a fever that broke. Your nervous system has been returned to baseline with surgical precision.

The shame is... there. But transformed. Where before it was a wall, now it's a window. You can see through it. On the other side: just yourself. Just a person in padding, in a dungeon, doing their best. And for the first time in longer than you can remember, *doing your best* feels like enough.

You stand up. The padding shifts. You notice it the way you notice shoes — present, functional, unremarkable. You take a step forward.

The mansion waits. You walk into it.

Not ashamed. Just... going.

There's a hair bow in your hair. You don't remember that. There's an enchanted diaper replacing what you were wearing. You definitely don't remember that. The siren is gone, leaving only the last few notes hanging in the air like dust.

Some part of you registered each change as it happened and thought it seemed reasonable at the time. The enchanted diaper — of course. The hair bow — naturally. The siren's song makes everything feel like a logical next step. The reasonable part wears off slowly.

You woke up to the last few notes still fading — soft, humid, wearing different clothes — and you couldn't quite be angry about it. That's the worst part. The anger arrives about ten minutes later, long after the melody has settled into something almost comfortable.

'Again and again, if that's what it takes. You'll learn.'
'Wrong? Look at yourself. Really look. Then tell me I'm wrong.'
'Smart. It goes easier when you stop pretending.'

*She gathers you up against her, and the heat rolls through you like the heaviest blanket in the world. Your eyes droop. Everything droops.*
Good little ember. *She rocks you, humming something slow, and you feel yourself melting.*
Soon, soon. First we get you ready for a nice long nap. *Crinkle. Tapes. A pacifier. A bow. You're too warm and heavy to argue.*
*She chuckles, a low rumble like a mountain settling.* There we go. Nothing to hold on to now. Just let it all go, sweetling.
*When you wake she's gone, and you're lying on warm rock in a thick, very used diaper, a paci in your mouth and a bow in your hair, with no memory of when exactly you stopped holding on.*

*The Ectoplasm Slime ripples with pale green light and emits a soft, eager gurgle.* Baba~
*Warm slime folds around your legs and hips in a slow, deliberate hug. Pressure builds deep inside your body.*
*The slime chirps happily and clings tighter, coating you in glowing residue that sinks through your clothes.*
*Every struggle only helps it spread. Your body feels heavier, fuller, and less willing to obey your commands.*
*A soft, phosphorescent snap answers you. Whatever it just fitted onto you is snug, thick, and very much not optional.*

Ectoplasm Slime catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'

The Ectoplasm Slime didn't just defeat you. It *absorbed* you — briefly — before depositing you back on the mansion floor in a way that suggested this was done with care, like a child putting down a toy.

Every inch of your skin is coated in slime. Warm, gently glowing, faintly sweet-smelling slime that clings to you like a second skin and sinks through clothing as if fabric were a suggestion. You can feel it working through your skin — not painfully, not aggressively, just with the patient, unstoppable thoroughness of osmosis. Seeping inward. Settling into your muscles. Communicating with your body in a chemical language you can't read but your organs apparently can.

Your stomach hears the message first. A deep, rolling, gurgling fullness blossoms behind your navel — the sensation of having drunk an enormous amount of warm liquid very quickly, except you haven't drunk anything, the slime delivered its payload transdermally.

Then your bladder hears the message. It responds immediately.

The slime generously left one contribution visible: the thick, padded garment that has been sealed around your hips while you were immersed. The ectoplasm has hardened just enough at the seams to make it load-bearing — not locked, not glued, but held with the quiet authority of something that expects to be needed and refuses to be removed prematurely. A ghostly onesie snaps over the top, its translucent front already showing the bulge beneath.

Your stomach gurgles — a long, low, liquid sound that travels downward with ominous momentum. The slime's moisture is pooling in every reservoir your body has, filling them past comfortable, past urgent, toward the kind of pressure that stops being a warning and starts being a countdown.

You press your hands against your abdomen. It's distended, warm, softly rounded with absorbed ectoplasmic fluid. Your body is a very full vessel with a compromised valve system and the ectoplasm is still processing.

The slime observes you from across the room with the patient, luminous gaze of something that put a lot of care into this moment and is enjoying every second of the payoff. *Baba~* it gurgles, softly.

You agree, apparently. Your body agrees loudly, warmly, and without your permission.

She vanishes in a puff of lavender smoke, leaving you standing in the aftermath of the hex's first and most devastating effect — knowing with terrible certainty that this will happen again. And again. And again. For twenty turns.

The air in the Dungeon doesn't smell of battle anymore; it smells of warm milk and powdered sugar, thick and cloying against your throat. The Nursery Witch doesn't gloat. She doesn't need to. She merely tilts her head, her eyes glowing with the soft, milky luminescence of a moon filtered through glass. When her fingers brush your forehead, the world doesn't break—it softens.

The sharp edges of your warrior's mind, the tactical calculations, the battle-hardened resolve, they all begin to melt like wax under a candle. A wave of dizziness washes over you, not from blood loss, but from a sudden, overwhelming desire to be held. Your knees, which had just been braced for a parry, buckle with a liquid weakness. You try to stand, but your center of gravity drags you down into a plush, oversized chair that seems to have materialized from the shadows.

The magic seeps into your marrow, whispering in a language of coos and lullabies. You feel your jaw unclench, your teeth feeling heavy in your mouth. The shame hits you first - a hot, prickling blush spreading down your neck to your chest, hotter than the feverish heat of a dragon's breath. You try to summon your battle cry, to roar at her, but your throat only produces a soft, breathy whimper. The magic is rewriting your history, turning the veteran into a dependent, and the sheer audacity of the transformation leaves you trembling. Your hands, usually gripping a weapon, are now fisting the fabric of your tunic, the texture soft and comforting in a way that feels dangerously wrong. You are losing the fight against your own biology, your mind sliding down a slippery slope of regression while the Witch watches with the gleeful precision of a tailor fitting a new suit.

"Forty turns," she whispers, her voice vibrating in the hollow of your ears, vibrating through your bones until your teeth ache. "Forty turns of sweet, helpless dependency. But first, the lock must be set."

She presses a cool, soft hand against your chest, right over your heart. The pressure isn't painful; it's an invitation to surrender. The shame delta spikes violently as you realize what she is demanding. It's not just submission; it is the physical release of your dignity to power the spell. Your body betrays you before your mind can agree. The infantile magic has rewired your nervous system, turning arousal into a desperate need for validation.

"Give it to me," she purrs, her fingers tracing the line of your spine. "Your pleasure is the seal. Your release is the chain."

The orgasm rips through you not like a spear, but like a tidal wave of pure, mindless bliss. It is a screaming, wordless cry that leaves your throat raw, your eyes rolling back as your body convulses in the chair. It is the most humiliating climax of your life, a surrender of the will that leaves you panting and slack-jawed. As the waves crash down, the magic flares, locking the hex into your very cells. The heat fades into a lingering, heavy warmth, leaving you feeling hollowed out and profoundly small.

The Witch steps back, smoothing her apron as the last wisp of lavender smoke curls around her. "There," she coos, patting your cheek with a hand that feels far too large. "Now you're mine. Try to stay dry, little one. We have forty turns to play."

She vanishes, leaving you shivering in the chair, the phantom weight of diapers settling over your hips, and the terrifying knowledge that for the next forty turns, you will have to beg to be taken care of.

The transition did not happen with a snap of light, but with a slow sinking, like a stone dropping into deep water. You found yourself kneeling on a floor of plush moss, the air thick with the scent of chamomile and ozone. Before you stood the Keeper, not with wings of silk, but draped in a cloak that seemed woven from twilight shadows. She held no weapon, only a garment that shimmered with a pearlescent sheen—a diaper woven from starlight and memory.

"You carry too much steel," she murmured, her voice resonating in your chest rather than your ears. "It is time to carry only the soft."

Her hands were ghostly cold as they gripped your waist, lifting you effortlessly as if gravity had lost its claim on you. The armor clattered away, discarded like shed skin. When she spread your legs, the air felt intimate, charged with static. As she slid the thick, padded layers between your thighs, the friction was not abrasive, but seductive. The magic hummed a low lullaby, vibrating through the fabric and into your bones. It felt less like clothing and more like a second skin, a heavy, comforting blanket for your lower half. She fastened the tabs with a soft *click* of enchantment, binding your legs together in a gentle, unyielding grip that demanded you sit or shuffle. "Let the weight settle," she whispered, pressing a cool finger to your forehead. "You will not need to stand again until the moon bleeds."

The silence of the nursery was absolute, save for the rustle of the garment around your hips. You tried to rise, but the magic had already rewritten your physiology. The diaper was no longer just padding; it was a vessel, expanding slightly with every shift of your hips. A warm, heavy pressure bloomed deep within your abdomen, a magical command that bypassed your will. You tried to hold it, to assert some shred of dignity, but the fabric seemed to drink the resistance.

*Thump.*

The sound was muffled, maddeningly loud in the quiet. The diaper swelled visibly, the padding glowing faintly with a soft, amber light as it absorbed the release. The heat spread outward, a cocoon of warmth against your skin that felt less like a stain and more like a blessing. You watched the Keeper retreat into the corners of the room, her eyes glowing like distant lanterns.

"Drink your fatigue," she called back, her voice echoing from everywhere and nowhere. "There is no shame in the fullness."

You slumped back against the mossy floor, the heavy bulk between your legs anchoring you to the earth. The magic pulsed in time with your heartbeat, a slow, rhythmic reminder that the struggle was over. You were no longer a warrior; you were a vessel, full and heavy, waiting for the sun to rise. The shame was gone, replaced by a drowsy, suffocating contentment. The diaper held you tighter than the dungeon ever could, and as your eyes closed, you realized the true trap was not the confinement, but the ease of letting go.
*The golem stands over you, glassy black and silent. It does not gloat. It does not move. It simply waits.*
*A heavy stone hand settles on your middle and presses. Gently. Firmly. It is very clear you are not going anywhere until it decides you are.*

actions.label: Please let me up, I need to go!

pages.text: *You make it about a foot. The golem takes one slow step and you are back where you started.*
*It considers this for a very long time. Then it reaches down and, with enormous care, tapes a printed diaper onto you. Problem solved, as far as it's concerned.*
*You wait. It waits. Eventually, so does your bladder, and then it doesn't. The golem lifts its hand at last, apparently satisfied.*
Obsidian Golem looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Obsidian Golem tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Obsidian Golem catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Obsidian Golem laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'
It let you up in the end. It just waited until it didn't matter any more. The printed diaper did its job, and you walk away very aware of it.
Your middle still aches where the stone hand pressed down. It pressed right where it would do the most harm, and now you need to go all the time.
It never said a word. Somehow that made it worse. You find yourself apologising to a rock on the way down the slope.
Obsidian Golem studies you with an unsettling sense of recognition. 'We've done this before, haven't we?'
'Your body remembers even if you won't admit it. I can see the evidence.'
'Again and again, if that's what it takes. You'll learn.'
'Wrong? Look at yourself. Really look. Then tell me I'm wrong.'
'Smart. It goes easier when you stop pretending.'

The wraith circles you in lazy loops, its hum threading between your thoughts like smoke through a keyhole. Something cool and smooth settles past your lips. You lift a hand to remove it — and find the ghostly onesie instead, soft and weightless and somehow already snapped shut. You don't remember putting it on.
You're sitting on the floor of the fog. The wraith is gone. The binkie is still there and you keep forgetting to take it out. The onesie doesn't feel wrong, which might be the worst part.

Between blinks the wraith is closer. You can't track it — it fades before your eyes adjust, reappears just behind you. The chant wraps around your ears like wool. Each time the wraith reappears, it's done something. You only catch fragments.
You come back to yourself in pieces. The ghostly onesie first, then the ghost bloomers, then the familiar weight in your mouth. The wraith is humming somewhere in the distance, satisfied.
The fog was thinning. You were almost through. And then the wraith began again — from the beginning of its song, patient and unhurried, like you hadn't made any progress at all.

Under your clothes — or rather, replacing what was under your clothes — a printed disposable diaper decorated with cheerful rocket ships has been taped on. Over it, electronic training pants hum with quiet, judgmental technology. The training pants contain a moisture sensor, a data recorder, and a small speaker that plays a musical jingle when... when.

The jingle played the moment the training pants snapped shut. Immediately. Before you'd done anything. The sensor detected 'pre-existing moisture' from the battle's stress and decided to celebrate.

The bot handed you a pamphlet before wheeling away. It's titled: ACCIDENTS HAPPEN (AND THAT'S OK!!!) in bright, child-friendly letters. Inside, a series of cartoon illustrations walk you through what to do when your training pants detect an 'event.'

Step 1: Don't panic! Your training pants are VERY absorbent!
Step 2: Find a Potty Trainer Bot for a check-up!
Step 3: Remember: every accident is a LEARNING OPPORTUNITY!
Step 4: Wouldn't it be easier to just let it happen? Think about it!

You stare at Step 4 for a long time. The training pants play their jingle again — a soft, electronic melody that you will hear in your nightmares.

Your bladder, stressed from the fight and destabilised by the bot's incontinence-bumping calibrations, sends a sharp pulse of urgency through your lower body. The training pants' sensor blinks from green to yellow.

WARNING: ELEVATED RISK DETECTED, the pants announce, to no one in particular.

You begin to waddle-run.

*RIBBIT.* The Puddle Toad hops onto your chest and settles there, heavy and cold and very pleased with itself.
*It leans in close and its throat puffs out. Underneath you, the puddle you landed in is soaking steadily through the seat of your clothes.*
*Ribbit.* (It is absolutely the tone of someone saying 'yes'.) *It kicks one more cold splash straight at your lap for emphasis.*
*The toad blinks slowly at the warm patch spreading through the cold water. Then it looks at you. It doesn't need to say anything. Nobody walking past will believe it was just the puddle either.*
*Satisfied, the toad plops back into its puddle with a smug little splash and leaves you to squelch your way back to the trail.*
Puddle Toad looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'
'Not ready?' Puddle Toad tilts their head. 'Sweetie, you were never going to be ready for me.'
'Shh. Save your energy. You'll need it for what comes after.'
'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Puddle Toad catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Puddle Toad laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

You sit up in the middle of the puddle with a gasp. The water is cold, autumn-cold, and it has soaked through everything below your waist. The chill climbs straight up into your belly and settles there, a tight, insistent ache.

You shiver. Your bladder shivers with you.

You try to stand, and the cold squeezes, and something lets go. A warm trickle spreads into the cold wet cloth, and for one confusing second it feels almost nice.

Then you remember where you are: in the middle of an open field, sitting in a puddle, very obviously wet. The toad croaks once from somewhere nearby, like a laugh.

aftermaths.title: Defeat - Puddle Toad (Variation B): Cold Feet

pages.text:
The toad has gone, but its puddle hasn't. Your socks squelch. Your shoes squelch. Every step back toward the trail sends a fresh splash of icy water up your legs, and each one tugs at your bladder like a hand on a string.

By the time you reach dry grass you're walking with your knees pressed together, and a farmer leaning on a fence watches you the whole way.

aftermaths.title: Defeat - Puddle Toad (Variation C): Just Puddle Water

pages.text:
"It's just puddle water," you tell the first traveller who looks at your soaked lap. They nod politely.

They do not believe you. You can tell because they step around you on the path, and because it is very clearly not just puddle water. It stopped being just puddle water somewhere around the third splash.
Puddle Toad studies you with an unsettling sense of recognition. 'We've done this before, haven't we?'
'Your body remembers even if you won't admit it. I can see the evidence.'
'Again and again, if that's what it takes. You'll learn.'
'Wrong? Look at yourself. Really look. Then tell me I'm wrong.'
'Smart. It goes easier when you stop pretending.'

*swivels in leather chair, steeples fingers* Ah, the intruder. I've been watching you on the monitors. Quite the journey through my facility.
You've seen the patients. The 'residents.' Some still fight it. Others have embraced the freedom of regression. Tell me — which group looked happier?
Chrysalis Corporation, Regression Research Division. I am its architect. Every injection, every serum, every sobbing patient rediscovering their... infantile self. All me.
*laughs* Ends? My dear child — and you WILL be my child, shortly — this is just the beginning. Phase 5 integration begins next week. Permanent isolation by quarter's end.
Prisoners with no responsibilities. No taxes. No heartbreak. Just warm bottles, soft padding, and someone who changes them when they need it. Is that really worse than YOUR life?
Your silence speaks volumes. Part of you already knows — the adult world is exhausting. Let go. My staff will take VERY good care of you. Starting now. *presses intercom*
Research Director looks you over with an expression that borders on pity. 'You came in here dressed like *that* and expected a different outcome?'
'Hold still. The less you fight this part, the faster it ends.'

'Smart. Now stay down and let this happen. Trust me -- you'll adjust.'
Research Director catches you before you hit the ground, almost gentle about it. 'There we go. Don't worry -- I know exactly what you need.'
'You can feel it already, can't you? That little flutter in your belly that says this is out of your hands now.'
Research Director laughs softly. 'Oh, by all means -- fight. It's my favourite part.'
'Deny it all you like. Your body already agreed with me.'
'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

The Director pressed a button.

You remember the button. A single, elegant control on the arm of his leather chair. He pressed it with one finger — his index finger, manicured, unhurried — and the world ended.

Not the actual world. Just yours.

White light. Pure, absolute, annihilating white. Every synapse in your brain firing simultaneously. Every memory of dignity, competence, and adulthood flashing before your eyes in a montage that felt like a eulogy.

Then darkness. Then a crib.

You're in a crib. The Director's private observation suite. Monitors on every wall show your vital signs, your brain activity, your incontinence metrics. All of them read the same thing: COMPLETE.

The full Chrysalis patient outfit was applied while you were unconscious. Hospital gown. Enormous diaper — the thickest, the heaviest, the most absorbent padding the facility produces. Puffy bloomers locked over the top with tabs you can't reach. Soft booties. A wristband reading PHASE 5 — COMPLETE. A pacifier that hums with chemical warmth and makes your jaw work in slow, helpless motions.

The diaper is already in use. Has been in use since you woke up. Has been in use since before you woke up. Your body emptied itself completely during the unconsciousness and the thick padding absorbed everything with the quiet efficiency of something designed for exactly this.

You try to stand. Your legs are jelly. You try to speak. Babble comes out — soft, formless sounds that were never words and don't pretend to be.

The Director watches from behind one-way glass, sipping something from a china cup. He makes a note on a leather-bound pad.

Global rollout by quarter's end, he'd said.

You are Patient Zero of Phase 5. The proof of concept. The data that will convince the Chrysalis board to fund worldwide deployment of the regression technology.

You sit in the crib. The pacifier hums. Your thoughts are cotton balls — soft, round, unable to hold shape. You understand less with each passing moment. The diaper fills and is changed by a nurse you don't have the cognitive function to recognise anymore. Fills again. Changed again. A cycle as natural and inevitable as breathing.

You try to remember your name. It's there, somewhere, in the fading architecture of a mind that used to be adult. But it's wrapped in so much fog, buried under so many layers of enforced regression, that reaching it feels like trying to grab smoke.

The monitors beep. The Director writes. The nurse changes you. The pacifier hums. The crib rocks slightly in its motorised cradle setting.

You were an adventurer.

You were.

The diaper is warm. The crib is warm. Everything is warm and soft and simple and you can't remember why that should bother you.

You close your eyes. The pacifier hums. Phase 5 is complete.

The Janitor doesn't even look at your face while he does it.

He's done this so many times that the whole process is muscle memory. Mop handle braced against the wall. Cart wheeled into position. Supply drawer opened. Your lower half stripped with the efficiency of someone handling a spill, not a person.

'There,' he says. 'Easier to clean up next time.'

Next time. The quiet certainty in those two words lands harder than any combat spell.

The Janitor's mop squeaks against the floor behind you. He's whistling. He knows something you don't want to accept yet.

The needle slid in before you could flinch.

'Just a little relaxant,' the School Nurse cooed, already pressing the plunger. The syringe was terrifyingly large and the liquid inside was pink.

Warmth. Immediate, spreading, unstoppable warmth, radiating outward from the injection site in your arm through your shoulder, down your chest, through your stomach, and into your lower body with the lazy, irresistible momentum of honey dripping from a spoon.

Your muscles unclenched. All of them. Starting at your jaw and cascading downward in a wave of enforced relaxation that you couldn't fight if you had a thousand years of training. Your bladder — clenched tight through the entire fight — simply... let go.

The nurse watched it happen with the clinical satisfaction of someone observing successful treatment. She had the diaper ready. She always has the diaper ready.

The medicine is permanent. That's the part that sits in your chest like a stone.

Not the diaper — the diaper can be changed, eventually, if you find one that fits. Not the wet mess currently pressed warm against your skin — that will dry, or be cleaned, or be absorbed by the thick medical padding she taped on you.

The medicine is permanent. Every loss to the School Nurse carves another notch in your continence, and those notches don't heal. Don't fade. Don't reverse. Each injection pushes your body a little further from 'adult' and a little closer to 'needs protection.'

You can feel it already. The relaxant didn't just release your bladder — it rewired it. Slightly. Permanently. The signals between your brain and your body's control mechanisms are a little fuzzier now, a little slower, a little less reliable.

The nurse smiles, caps the syringe, and makes a note in your chart: 'Treatment administered. Patient progressing nicely.'

Progressing. Toward what, exactly?

You look down at the thick diaper taped around your hips. Your body answers the question before your mind can.

*A dark shape flutters in the gloom. Its wings drip with shadow.* ...another one who thinks they're too grown-up for my gifts.
I am what happens when a Diaper Fairy stops being nice. The shadows showed me the TRUTH: everyone is just a baby pretending to be big. And I'm here to help you stop pretending.
Oh, I'm STILL a fairy. Just... improved. The regular fairies give you pretty diapers and hair bows. I give you cobwebs and nightmares. Much more honest, wouldn't you say?
Shhhh. The shadows don't lie. *Dark tendrils wrap around you, tugging at your clothes.* By the time I'm done, you'll look exactly like you're supposed to. Small. Padded. Helpless.
The shadows are the only mercy you'll get. They'll hide the worst of it. No one will see you waddle home... well, no one except me. *a cruel giggle echoes in the dark*

'Please? That's a start. We'll work on the rest.'

Darkness has a texture, you discover. It's cool and slightly damp and it moves against your skin like breath.

The Shadow Fairy's tendrils stripped you bare with clinical precision and then rebuilt you from scratch. Cobweb padding wraps your hips — the same living, breathing enchanted silk the elder witches weave, but darker, infused with shadow magic that makes it shimmer between visible and invisible depending on the light. A ghostly onesie hangs from your shoulders, translucent enough to show the thick outline of the diaper beneath. Bramble-and-thorn headwear tangles in your hair. Wet moss boots squelch on your feet with every step.

And then there's the plug. The mushroom plug. It slid into place during the darkness with a terrible, organic warmth, and it sits there now — firm, immovable, filling — while the shadow magic ensures your body can't expel it.

The Shadow Fairy said something true, before the darkness took you. She said everyone is just a baby pretending to be big.

Standing here in the Forest of the Seam — padded in cobwebs beneath a ghostly onesie, plugged, booted in moss, with thorns in your hair and twenty more points of incontinence carved into your body — you feel the truth of it pressing against your chest.

You're not pretending very well anymore.

The mushroom plug shifts when you move, sending deep waves of pressure through your abdomen. The cobweb diaper crinkles-whispers in a voice too low to be heard. Your bladder screams. Your body is already losing the fight — you can feel warmth beginning to migrate without your permission, finding the path of least resistance, which is now the only path your body has.

The shadows watch. They always watch. And in the dark, no one can see you waddle.

Standing here in the Forest of the Seam — padded in cobwebs beneath a ghostly onesie, plugged, booted in moss, with thorns in your hair and twenty more points of incontinence carved into your body — you feel the truth of it pressing against your chest.
